pharm: Major intracellular thiol antioxidant and detoxifying agent; used as a supplement and, off-label, for skin lightening and as adjunctive antioxidant therapy
summary: Glutathione is an endogenous tripeptide (gamma-glutamyl-cysteinyl-glycine) that is the principal intracellular antioxidant and a key substrate in phase II detoxification and free-radical scavenging. It is marketed as an oral, intravenous or topical supplement and is widely used off-label for skin lightening and as adjunctive antioxidant therapy, though high-quality efficacy and safety data, especially for intravenous and skin-lightening use, are lacking. Oral bioavailability is limited. It is not FDA-approved for these uses; the FDA and several health authorities have warned against unapproved injectable glutathione for skin whitening.
indications: Adjunctive antioxidant support in some chemotherapy or hepatic conditions (investigational)

dosage.n: Not approved; safety/efficacy unproven, IV use discouraged

admin: Take oral doses with or without food
Do not use unregulated injectable glutathione for cosmetic skin lightening
Use products from reputable sources, as supplement quality varies
Follow product-specific instructions for topical or oral forms
moa: Acts as the major intracellular antioxidant: its reactive thiol group neutralizes reactive oxygen species and electrophiles, regenerates other antioxidants (vitamins C and E), and serves as a cofactor for glutathione peroxidases and glutathione-S-transferases in detoxification. The proposed skin-lightening effect is attributed to inhibition of tyrosinase and a shift from eumelanin to pheomelanin synthesis.

monitor: Injection-site or infusion reactions if IV used

preg: Avoid; there are insufficient data to establish safety in pregnancy.
lact: Avoid; there are insufficient data to establish safety during breastfeeding.
renal: No specific data; use with caution in significant renal impairment.
hepatic: No specific data; use with caution in significant hepatic impairment.

moderate: Chemotherapy agents (e.g. cisplatin) - theoretical reduction of cytotoxic efficacy; use only under oncology guidance
minor: Other antioxidants - additive antioxidant effect of uncertain significance
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol, which increases oxidative stress and depletes glutathione
interactions.diagnostics: No well-characterized effects on routine laboratory tests

serious: Severe skin reactions reported with unapproved IV use (e.g. Stevens-Johnson syndrome)
Possible thyroid dysfunction with prolonged high-dose use
Renal or hepatic dysfunction reported with unregulated IV use
rare: Toxic epidermal necrolysis (reported with IV use)
emergency: Acute infusion reaction with IV use

monitoring: Renal, hepatic and thyroid function with prolonged high-dose or IV use
counsel: Oral glutathione is poorly absorbed; benefits are uncertain
Do not use injectable glutathione for skin whitening - it is unapproved and may be unsafe
Tell your doctor if you are receiving chemotherapy before using antioxidant supplements
Stop and seek care if you develop rash, swelling or breathing difficulty
Choose reputable products and avoid unregulated injectables
pk: Oral absorption is low and variable
Plasma half-life very short (minutes) when given systemically
Below 25 C, dry place; protect from light and moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved for skin lightening or systemic disease; FDA has warned against unapproved injectable glutathione
Oral bioavailability is poor due to gastrointestinal breakdown
Marketed widely as a supplement; high-quality clinical evidence is limited
Unregulated IV use carries risks of severe skin reactions and infection
Pending clinical review for FDA status
missed: Take the missed supplement dose when remembered, or skip it if it is nearly time for the next dose; do not double up.
overdose: Overdose data are limited; large oral amounts may cause gastrointestinal upset. Management is supportive; there is no specific antidote.
refs: FDA / Health authority warnings on unapproved injectable glutathione (skin whitening)
